findings.title: CLU reports raw cache_lines COUNT as Cache-Line-Utilization (valid=true) — inverse of the true metric
findings.scenario: The codebase's own CLU definition (axis_05_memory_layout_observable.hpp:118-120) is the ratio field_bytes/(cache_lines*64) from the real store footprint; the thesis term is 'Cache-Line-AUSLASTUNG' (03_messsystem_prtart.tex:383). ObserverSnapshotSystemAxis instead copies axis_stats[5][3] (absolute count of touched 64-B lines) and marks it valid. Concrete failure: same dataset (identical field_bytes), layout A packs keys into 50 lines (utilization ~1.0), layout B scatters them over 200 lines (utilization ~0.25). Reported 'CLU': A=50, B=200 — an evaluation/heuristic consumer ranks B as 4x BETTER cache-line utilization although it is 4x worse; the value also grows with workload size, so CLU comparisons across run lengths are meaningless. This is exactly the mislabeling ('Phantomwert-Etikett') the same file's honest-0 percentile handling forbids; the honest value needs axis_stats[5][2] (field_bytes) AND [5][3], or must be invalidated.

findings.title: FILL_BUFFER_OCCUPANCY mislabeled: software T17 Operations-Puffer peak_size sold as hardware fill-buffer occupancy
findings.scenario: The thesis derives the category 'Fill-Buffer-Auslastung' (03_state_of_the_art.tex:543) from Mahling P25 fill-buffer-aware prefetching, i.e. CPU line-fill buffers, and states these hardware quantities need counters/simulators 'wo reale Zaehler fehlen (P25 Mahling)' (03_state_of_the_art.tex:515-517). T17 queuing_q1 is per thesis a software 'Operations-Puffer' (Disruptor-Ring, SPSC/MPMC; 03_messsystem_prtart.tex:85, 04_concept_architecture.tex:105) whose puts/gets are auto-coupled to tier_insert/lookup counts (abi_adapter.hpp:1279). Concrete failure: a prefetch-axis sweep (PF variants around P25) that saturates the ~10-12 hardware LFBs changes FILL_BUFFER_OCCUPANCY not at all — q1.peak_size depends only on the insert/lookup op mix — while a workload with more inserts inflates it without any LFB pressure; the category returns valid=true for a physically unrelated value (phantom value against the honest-0 doctrine). Additionally peak_size is an absolute element count, not an 'Auslastung/Occupancy' (no capacity normalization).

findings.title: MEMORY_FOOTPRINT uses current bytes_in_use instead of the thesis-canonical peak (bytes_in_use_peak)
findings.scenario: The thesis canonical measurement record specifies the Speicher-Feld 'bytes_in_use_peak' (05_evaluation.tex:94-95). axis_stats[6][1] is the allocator's CURRENT balance: it is decremented on every deallocate (verified in axis_06_allocator_hoard.hpp:104-107, same for the other allocator strategies). Concrete failure: a mixed workload with an erase/teardown phase before the observer snapshot (e.g. Messreihe with insert->erase cycles) reports a footprint near 0 with valid=true, although peak memory in use was megabytes — the footprint comparison between an in-place layout and a CoW-heavy layout (whose peak is far above its end-state) is systematically distorted in favor of the CoW variant.

findings.title: ENERGY_J sample carries micro-joules unconverted under a category named Joules
findings.scenario: PmcSystemAxis copies PmcCounters::energy_micro_joules (unit: uJ, per pmc_source.hpp:26) into a sample whose category is ENERGY_J (unit suffix: Joules); SystemAxisSample has no unit field and system_axis.hpp documents no uJ convention at the collect site. Concrete failure: an evaluation consumer that trusts the category name (e.g. csv_to_latex Steckbrief printing 'Energie [J]') reports 99000 J instead of 0.099 J — a factor-10^6 error in every energy figure of the thesis measurement chapters. Either document/rename the unit at the sample contract or convert.

result.reason: Confirmed at real code. system_axis.hpp:257 copies axis_stats[5][3] with valid=true under case MeasurementCategory::CLU; kV3AxisSchema (observable_tier.hpp, T5 memory_layout = {scan, records, field_bytes, cache_lines, checksum}) proves [5][3] is the raw accumulated count of touched 64-B cache lines, not a utilization. The codebase's own authoritative definition (axis_05_memory_layout_observable.hpp, observe_real_footprint doc, P-MD1-ERDUNG #167) states verbatim 'CLU = field_bytes/(cache_lines*64)'; measurement_category.hpp:10 names the category Cache-Line-Utilization. Reporting raw cache_lines as CLU is semantically inverted (scattered layout: more lines touched => higher reported 'CLU' though true utilization is lower) and workload-size-dependent, and the honest ratio cannot be reconstructed downstream because field_bytes (axis_stats[5][2]) is not exported by ObserverSnapshotSystemAxis at all. This contradicts the same file's own honest-0 doctrine (lines 227-229 mean-as-percentile and line 317 IPC_CPI are invalidated as 'Phantomwert', while the equally mislabeled CLU gets valid=true). The dossier spec does not sanction the raw-count mapping, and the new contract test (test_m_contract_system_axis_wurzel.cpp:115,124-126, comment 'CLU host proxy', EXPECT_EQ(clu.value, 64u)) locks in the wrong semantics.

The uJ pass-through at system_axis.hpp:312 is spec-conformant, documented, and harmless in the real codebase. (1) The claimed failure requires a consumer that maps ENERGY_J to a 'J' unit label — no such consumer exists anywhere in the repo (no csv_to_latex, no Steckbrief, no category-to-unit mapping; all real energy exports use the explicit column name energy_micro_joules). (2) The header DOES document the convention: line 69 states 'ENERGY_J ist code-verankert ueber PmcCounters::energy_micro_joules', anchoring the category to the uJ field. (3) The authoritative CODEX-DOSSIER spec prescribes exactly this binding ('ENERGY_J [PmcCounters.energy]', 'Werte exakt' in the contract test), and the locked test expects raw 99000 pass-through. (4) The proposed conversion to J would truncate the uint64_t value (99000 uJ -> 0 J), destroying realistic RAPL deltas and violating the file's honest-0 doctrine — the fix would introduce a real bug. The naming tension lives in the pre-existing ENERGY_J enum (unmodified F1 code), not in this increment; no demonstrable failure exists.

Trace fully reproduced. system_axis.hpp:257 (ObserverSnapshotSystemAxis::do_collect) copies snapshot->axis_stats[5][3] into the CLU sample and sets valid=true. Per kV3AxisSchema (observable_tier.hpp:75, T5 memory_layout fields scan/records/field_bytes/cache_lines/checksum) index [5][3] is the raw cumulative count of touched 64-B cache lines (MemoryLayoutSnapshot::cache_lines_touched, accumulated with += per scan/chunk in axis_05_memory_layout_observable.hpp:111/128). CLU's documented semantics is Cache-Line-Utilization (measurement_category.hpp:10), defined in the codebase itself as the ratio field_bytes/(cache_lines*64) (axis_05_memory_layout_observable.hpp:119-120) and in the thesis as Cache-Line-Auslastung (03_messsystem_prtart.tex:383). At fixed field_bytes the ratio is strictly decreasing in cache_lines, so the reported raw count is anti-monotone to the true metric: packed layout A (50 lines, util ~1.0) reports 50, scattered layout B (200 lines, util ~0.25) reports 200 — a consumer ranking by the CLU label inverts the ordering (prefers the 4x worse layout). Being an unnormalized accumulator, the value also grows with workload length, making cross-run CLU comparison meaningless. This contradicts the same file's honest-0 doctrine (lines 227-229 and 317 invalidate instead of emitting mislabeled 'Phantomwerte'), and the honest inputs (axis_stats[5][2]=field_bytes plus [5][3]) are available in the snapshot. The CODEX-DOSSIER does not mandate the raw-count mapping; no counter-evidence that raw cache_lines is an intended CLU definition.

Confirmed at the real code. system_axis.hpp:261 reports axis_stats[6][1] as MEMORY_FOOTPRINT with valid=true. That cell is contract-bound to "bytes_in_use" (kV3AxisSchema T6, observable_tier.hpp:76) and filled from AllocationStatistics::total_bytes_in_use (abi_adapter.hpp:1101-1102), a current balance decremented on every deallocate in all allocator strategies (hoard.hpp:104-107, michael_lf:106-109, numalloc:120-123, vampir_nfp:116-119); AllocationStatistics has no peak member and no running-max exists anywhere in the chain. The thesis-canonical Mess-Record specifies the Speicher-Feld bytes_in_use_peak (05_evaluation.tex DE:95/EN:94). Hence a workload with an erase/teardown phase before the observer snapshot yields a near-0 footprint marked valid, systematically distorting footprint comparisons (e.g. in-place vs. CoW-heavy layouts). This also violates the file's own honest-0 doctrine, which invalidates LATENCY_P50-P999 and IPC_CPI for exactly analogous semantic mismatches; the pre-existing measurement_snapshot.hpp:107 mislabel ([6][1] -> bytes_in_use_peak) shares the root cause but does not excuse the new code.

Full trace reproduced. system_axis.hpp:261 serves MEMORY_FOOTPRINT from axis_stats[6][1] with valid=true; kV3AxisSchema (observable_tier.hpp:76) names that field "bytes_in_use" and T6 has no peak column; the sole writer fill_observer_v3 (abi_adapter.hpp:1102) stores AllocationStatistics::total_bytes_in_use, which is decremented on every deallocate (verified axis_06_allocator_hoard.hpp:104-107; the strategies share the same struct, which has no peak field at all). The thesis-canonical Mess-Record (de/05_evaluation.tex:94-95) specifies the Speicher-Feld as bytes_in_use_peak. Hence an insert->erase workload snapshotted after teardown reports a near-0 footprint as valid=true although peak usage was megabytes, systematically favoring end-state-lean (e.g. CoW-heavy) layouts. The bug also contradicts the file's own honest-0 doctrine, which in the very same file invalidates mislabeled means-as-percentiles (lines 223-230) and missing IPC_CPI fields (315-319); current-balance-as-peak is the same phantom-value class and should be invalidated or the peak plumbed through the POD.

The mechanics are as described (system_axis.hpp:312 copies PmcCounters::energy_micro_joules raw into an ENERGY_J-category sample; no unit field on SystemAxisSample), but the failure trace does not carry. (1) The claimed consumer is fictional: the only SystemAxisSample consumer in both repos is the new contract test; csv_to_latex never touches SystemAxisSample or MeasurementCategory::ENERGY_J — it parses a CSV column literally named 'energy_micro_joules' (csv_to_latex.hpp:38, .cpp:96) and its only energy output is the Steckbrief line 'Energy = 0 / nicht erhoben' (.cpp:675/757); it prints no 'Energie [J]'. (2) The real thesis energy chain is uJ-named end to end (measurement_snapshot.hpp:146/159, result_aggregator.cpp:65/72, cache_engine_builder_iterator.hpp:249/426, module_abi_v1.hpp:38, latex_anhang/main.cpp:39), so a 10^6 error in thesis energy figures cannot arise from this increment. (3) The uJ anchoring IS documented in the same file (system_axis.hpp:69: 'ENERGY_J ist code-verankert ueber PmcCounters::energy_micro_joules') and locked in by the test (99000 in → 99000 out). (4) Converting to integer Joules in the uint64_t value field would truncate 99000 uJ to 0 — raw uJ passthrough is the only lossless choice; the '_J' enum name is pre-existing (F1), not introduced here. Residual: a documentation-polish nit (state the uJ convention at the SystemAxisSample contract/collect site), not a real defect with a reproducible failure.

Confirmed at the real code. system_axis.hpp:264-267 maps FILL_BUFFER_OCCUPANCY to snapshot->axis_stats[17][4] with valid=true; per kV3AxisSchema (observable_tier.hpp:98) that field is T17 queuing_q1.peak_size, a software operations-buffer peak element count whose put/get are auto-coupled to tier_insert/lookup (abi_adapter.hpp:1279-1288, queue impls track max data_.size()). The thesis defines Fill-Buffer exclusively as the P25-Mahling hardware line-fill-buffer concept (03_state_of_the_art.tex:242 under 'Hardware-nahe Organe', :515-517, :543) and calls T17 an 'Operations-Puffer' (03_messsystem_prtart.tex:85); the codebase itself encodes fill-buffer=P25 hardware (permutation_flags.hpp:126 FILL_BUFFER_AWARE // P25). The category list at 03_messsystem_prtart.tex:383-385 does not even include Fill-Buffer among observer-resolvable categories. Failure scenario holds: LFB saturation leaves the value unchanged while insert-heavy workloads inflate it — a phantom value returned valid=true, contradicting the honest-0 doctrine the same file applies to latency percentiles (line 227-229) and IPC_CPI (line 317). Secondary point also valid: peak_size is an absolute count, not a capacity-normalized occupancy (the real avg_occupancy double was deliberately excluded from the POD, observable_tier.hpp:64-65). No refutation found: the dossier prescribes only 'FILL_BUFFER from snapshot' without legitimizing this field, and unlike CLU/MEMORY_FOOTPRINT the source is not a semantic proxy.

Trace fully reproduced. system_axis.hpp:264-267 maps FILL_BUFFER_OCCUPANCY to snapshot->axis_stats[17][4] with valid=true; per kV3AxisSchema (observable_tier.hpp:98) that slot is T17 queuing_q1 'peak_size', written by abi_adapter.hpp's T17 block which is 'AUTO-gekoppelt via tier_insert/lookup put/get' (r[4]=q.peak_size) — a software Operations-Puffer (Disruptor-Ring/SPSC/MPMC per thesis 03_messsystem_prtart.tex:85, 04_concept_architecture.tex:105) peak element count driven solely by the insert/lookup op mix. The thesis category derives from Mahling P25 fill-buffer(=CPU line-fill-buffer)-aware prefetching (03_state_of_the_art.tex:242/543; glossary 'P25 Mahling 2025 (Fill Buffer)') and names P25 among the hardware quantities needing counters/simulators 'wo reale Zaehler fehlen' (515-517); the bridge passage the code itself cites (03:382-386) omits Fill-Buffer from the observer-resolved subset, so the TimeObserver classification is unbacked. Failure scenario holds: LFB saturation leaves the value unchanged, insert-heavy workloads inflate it without any LFB pressure, yet valid=true is returned — a phantom value contradicting the honest-0 doctrine applied in the same file to IPC_CPI (line 315-319) and latency percentiles (line 223-230), which are invalidated for exactly this reason. Secondary point also correct: peak_size is an absolute count, not a capacity-normalized occupancy. The dossier specified only 'FILL_BUFFER aus dem Snapshot' without naming a field; the queuing_q1.peak_size choice is implementation-introduced and the new test (test_m_contract_system_axis_wurzel.cpp:132-134) locks the phantom in. findings.title: Neues Test-Target ohne per-Target COMDARE_CE_ENABLE_STATISTICS/COMDARE_MEASUREMENT_ON — Build-Bruch in RELEASE_MODE-/STATISTICS=OFF-Konfiguration
findings.scenario: Der neue CMake-Endblock nutzt add_executable ohne die per-Target-Defines, die das Schwester-Target test_cmd1_a_axis_command_base explizit setzt (tests/unit/CMakeLists.txt:1842-1843: COMDARE_MEASUREMENT_ON=1 COMDARE_CE_ENABLE_STATISTICS=1). Konfiguriert man mit -DCOMDARE_RELEASE_MODE=ON (erzwingt COMDARE_CE_ENABLE_STATISTICS=OFF, Top-CMakeLists.txt:121) oder -DCOMDARE_CE_ENABLE_STATISTICS=OFF, entfaellt das globale add_compile_definitions; StdMalloc hat dann kein statistics() (axis_06_allocator_std_malloc.hpp, #ifdef-gated) und ist nicht ObservableAxis, wodurch MeasurementVisitable<StdMalloc, NoMeasurementVisitor&> trivial true wird. Reproduziert: g++ -std=c++23 ohne das Define bricht mit 'test_m_contract_system_axis_wurzel.cpp:74:15: error: static assertion failed' (static_assert(!topics::MeasurementVisitable<alloc::StdMalloc, NoMeasurementVisitor&>)); mit -DCOMDARE_CE_ENABLE_STATISTICS=1 kompiliert die TU (EXIT 0). Zusaetzlich wuerde der Runtime-Test MeasurementVisitableConstrainsObservableVisitors (erwartet observable_count==1) in dieser Konfiguration semantisch kippen. Fix: target_compile_definitions wie bei test_cmd1_a setzen (oder comdare_add_test-Konvention nutzen).

findings.title: ObserverSnapshotSystemAxis koppelt sich per Magic-Index (axis_stats[5][3]/[6][1]/[17][4]) an das Organ-Achsen-Schema statt compile-time an kV3AxisSchema — stille Phantomwerte bei Schema-Drift
findings.scenario: Die Zeilen 257/261/265 lesen snapshot->axis_stats[5][3] (memory_layout.cache_lines), [6][1] (allocator.bytes_in_use), [17][4] (queuing_q1.peak_size) nur mit Kommentar-Bindung. kV3AxisSchema in anatomy/observable_tier.hpp ist als Single-Source-Vertrag dokumentiert ('diese Tabelle IST der Vertrag ... keine Namens-Drift') und wird im selben Header bereits included — eine constexpr-Namens-Lookup-Funktion bzw. static_assert(kV3AxisSchema[5].names[3] == "cache_lines"sv etc.) waere moeglich, fehlt aber. Konkretes Fehl-Szenario: eine kuenftige Schema-Aenderung (die Tabelle antizipiert explizit weitere Phase-B-Felder/Umordnungen) verschiebt cache_lines/bytes_in_use/peak_size an eine andere Spalte; CLU/MEMORY_FOOTPRINT/FILL_BUFFER_OCCUPANCY liefern dann stumm falsche Werte mit valid=true (Phantomwert wider die im Diff selbst betonte honest-0-Doktrin), waehrend test_m_contract_system_axis_wurzel.cpp gruen bleibt, weil der Test dieselben Magic-Indizes hartkodiert (Zeilen 118-120). Aktuell verifiziert stimmen die Indizes; der Defekt ist die fehlende compile-time-Absicherung des Vertrags, nicht ein heutiger Falschwert.

result.reason: Verified at the real code: system_axis.hpp:257/261/265 hardcode axis_stats[5][3]/[6][1]/[17][4] with comment-only binding; grep confirms the header never references kV3AxisSchema despite including observable_tier.hpp (line 9), so no static_assert/constexpr lookup guards the mapping although the schema is inline constexpr and directly checkable. The indices currently match the schema (T5.names[3]=cache_lines, T6.names[1]=bytes_in_use, T17.names[4]=peak_size), exactly as the claim states. kV3AxisSchema is documented as the single-source contract ("diese Tabelle IST der Vertrag ... keine Namens-Drift") and explicitly anticipates Phase-B field additions/reserve columns; the established consumers (cache_engine_builder_iterator.hpp:219/381, test_obs_phaseA.cpp) read schema-driven by name and boast "NICHT hartkodiert" — the new axis is the sole index-hardcoded consumer. The unit test (actual lines 115-117, claim said 118-120 — trivial offset) hardcodes the same indices, so a schema reorder yields silently wrong values with valid=true while tests stay green, contradicting the honest-0 doctrine the same diff enforces elsewhere (percentile/IPC_CPI invalidation). Missing compile-time contract enforcement is a genuine, refutation-surviving finding.

Verified end-to-end: system_axis.hpp:257/261/265 hardcode axis_stats[5][3]/[6][1]/[17][4] with comment-only binding, while kV3AxisSchema (observable_tier.hpp:66-101, already included at system_axis.hpp:9) is the documented single-source contract ('diese Tabelle IST der Vertrag ... keine Namens-Drift') and is inline constexpr with string-literal names — a static_assert(string_view{kV3AxisSchema[5].names[3]}=="cache_lines") etc. would compile today but is absent. Current indices match (T5.names[3]=cache_lines, T6.names[1]=bytes_in_use, T17.names[4]=peak_size), so no wrong value today; the defect is the missing compile-time guard. The failure scenario holds concretely: the schema explicitly anticipates further fields/reordering (observable_tier.hpp:50 'schema-stabil gegen weitere Felder (Phase B)'; project doctrine allows schema breaks), and on any index shift CLU/MEMORY_FOOTPRINT/FILL_BUFFER_OCCUPANCY would silently return a different counter with valid=true (phantom value against the honest-0 doctrine this same header enforces for percentiles and IPC_CPI), while test_m_contract_system_axis_wurzel.cpp stays green because it hardcodes the identical magic indices (snapshot.axis_stats[5][3]=64 etc.). Drift-latent contract-enforcement gap introduced by this increment, correctly framed by the claim.

findings.title: MeasurementVisitable erzwingt AxisCommand<Axis> und bricht damit alle Bestands-Aufrufer mit Organ-Huellen-Achsen: anatomy_execution_context.hpp:167 (observe_all) kompiliert im DEFAULT-Build nicht mehr
findings.scenario: Compiler-CONFIRMED (g++ 16, C++23): AnatomyExecutionContext<ArtComposition>::observe_all() mit COMDARE_CE_ENABLE_STATISTICS=1 (Root-CMakeLists.txt:133-137, Option default ON, global via add_compile_definitions) instanziieren -> anatomy_execution_context.hpp:167 'no matching function ... constraints not satisfied ... AxisBaseConcept'. Ursache: MeasurementVisitable = AxisCommand<Axis> && (...); AxisCommand verlangt get_compiler()/is_original_module()/name(), aber Composition::search_algo ist fuer ALLE Referenz-Kompositionen (art/hot/masstree/wormhole/prt_art *_reference.hpp) die Organ-Huelle ObservableComposedContainer<...> (observable_composed_container.hpp:56), die KEINE dieser statischen Methoden hat und nicht von AxisBase erbt. Gegenprobe: identischer Aufruf mit der alten, unconstrained Form von axis_accept_measurement kompiliert sauber (Exit 0) -> echte Rueckwaertskompatibilitaets-Regression, kein Altbestandsfehler. Konkret betroffen: tests/unit/test_v41_anatomy_f15_measurement.cpp TEST Saeule2_PerAxisStatisticsTraceRealOrgan (Z.236-269, ruft ctx.observe_all() fuer Art/Hot/Masstree) -- die TU bricht im Default-Build hart. Fix-Richtung: entweder AxisCommand-Konjunkt aus MeasurementVisitable nehmen (nur den Visitor-Vertrag pruefen) oder die Organ-Huellen AxisBase+name() nachruesten.

findings.title: Ungeguardete static_assert(!MeasurementVisitable<StdMalloc, NoMeasurementVisitor&>) bricht den unterstuetzten Build mit COMDARE_CE_ENABLE_STATISTICS=OFF
findings.scenario: Compiler-CONFIRMED: TU ohne -DCOMDARE_CE_ENABLE_STATISTICS=1 kompilieren -> 'static assertion failed' in Zeile 74, weil ObservableAxis<StdMalloc> nur mit Statistics-Macro gilt (statistics()/observer() sind #ifdef'd); ohne Macro ist StdMalloc nicht observable, MeasurementVisitable wird trivially true, Assert feuert. Konkreter Konfig-Pfad: cmake -DCOMDARE_CE_ENABLE_STATISTICS=OFF (erste-Klasse-Option 'Production-Export', Root-CMakeLists.txt:133) oder -DCOMDARE_RELEASE_MODE=ON (erzwingt STATISTICS=OFF, Z.121) bei COMDARE_BUILD_TESTS=ON (default ON, Z.32, wird von RELEASE_MODE NICHT abgeschaltet) -> Test-Suite-Build bricht beim Kompilieren dieser TU. 26 Geschwister-Testdateien guarden COMDARE_CE_ENABLE_STATISTICS per #ifdef (z.B. test_v41_anatomy_f15_measurement.cpp mit GTEST_SKIP); die neue TU (Z.73-75 static_asserts + TEST Z.179-186) hat keinen Guard, und der neue CMake-Block (tests/unit/CMakeLists.txt:2493-2510) setzt das Define auch nicht per-Target.
